pages.text:
Heats a receiver with the sun: up to 600 HU/t at 1,100°C at clear noon. The temperature follows the sun: above 500°C (High-Pressure Steam) from about 7:45 to 16:15 in clear weather, and above 900°C (a Superheater Array, or Superheated Steam) from about 9:40 to 14:20.
# Building
A 2x2 tower 4 tall: three layers of Solar Thermal Array Casings with one controller in the bottom layer, facing out, and four Solar Collectors on top. Formed, it becomes a tower with a trough mirror on top that follows the sun.
The controller's facing is the tracking axis: north or south for the north-south axis (full output), east or west for east-west (x0.7).

# Sun and weather
The output follows the sun's height: nothing at night, about 70% by mid-morning, full at noon. Rain and snow cut it to 30%; in a thunderstorm the trough stows face down and gets 10%. Deserts, badlands and savannas give 20% more, cold biomes 15% less. Each collector that can't see the sky loses a quarter.
The receiver is only as hot as the sun allows, so High-Pressure Steam comes only around midday in clear weather, and not on the east-west axis.
# Heat out
Through heat ports, at its whole output even into a touching machine: a new tower has one on the bottom block behind the controller. Set more with the Wrench in Port mode.
One array gives less heat than a boiler can boil, so set the boiler's pressure to High-Pressure to hold it at 500°C.
